1: Daily Study Bible · False Prophets · v.1

Barclay says false prophets in the church were only to be expected, since they had led God’s people astray in every generation, and that “heresy” first meant simply a line of belief a person had chosen.
This sect is called heresy in Latin, in Greek it is called hairesis, when someone, with foolish obstinacy, never ceases to follow the errors they have once adopted.

Barclay finds four things to notice about the false teachers and their teaching in these two verses.
Says false teachers may be popular, and that a crowd of followers does not show that something is of God.

The way of truth will be blasphemed by heretics not only in those whom they draw out to associate with their heresy, but also in those whom by their most impure deeds and sacrifices, or the execrable mysteries they perform, they provoke to hatred of the Christian name, those who are unskilled thinking all Christians to be entangled in such wickedness.
3: Says false teachers work through covetousness, their own and their followers’, and that their judgment is not idle.
